Petitioners are accused Nos.1 to 4 in Crime No.915 of 2020 of Cherpu Police Station, Thrissur District which is now pending as C.C.No.10 of 2021 before the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Thrissur.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Thrissur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The petitioners face allegations of having committed the offences punishable under Sections 416, 417, 418, 419, 376 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
2. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioners would submit that all issues between the petitioners and the 2nd respondent have been settled.

It is submitted that the allegation is that the petitioners with the intention to create loss to the 2nd respondent (who is the wife of the 1 st petitioner), after hiding the fact that the 1 st petitioner has hearing impairment for his left ear and earlier had illicit relation with another lady, made the 2 nd respondent to marry the 1st petitioner and thereby deceived and cheated her causing injury and loss to her.

The learned counsel Crl.M.C.
NO.3862 OF 2021 would submit that all issues between the petitioners and the 2nd respondent have been settled and they do not wish to continue with the prosecution in any manner.

3. The learned Public Prosecutor and the learned counsel appearing for the 2nd respondent would confirm that all issues between the petitioners and the 2 nd respondent have been settled and they do not wish to continue with the prosecution in any manner.

4. Having heard the learned counsel for the petitioners, the learned Public Prosecutor and the learned counsel for the 2nd respondent, I am of the view that the proceedings against the petitioners can be terminated in exercise of the jurisdiction vested in this Court under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.
No public interest will be served by continuing with the proceedings against the petitioners.
The nature of the offences does not compel me to hold that the proceedings cannot be quashed on the ground of settlement.

Keeping the principles laid down by the Supreme Court in Gian Singh v. State of Punjab and Crl.M.C. NO.3862 OF 2021 Another; [(2012) 10 SCC 303)], and State of Madhya Pradesh v.
Laxmi Narayan and Others; [(2019) 5 SCC 688], I am of the view that considering the nature of the offences alleged against the petitioners, the proceedings can be quashed on the basis of settlement.
